candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — skin-cancer prevention / sun-safety teaching
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients when solar UV exposure tends to be strongest and reinforce that cloud cover does not eliminate UV exposure.

options.D: UV intensity does not vary with time of day

candidate.rationale: CDC states that in the continental United States, UV rays tend to be strongest from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. during daylight saving time (9 a.m. to 3 p.m. during standard time). Therefore A is correct. UV exposure also occurs on cloudy and cool days, and intensity varies with time of day.
candidate.source_claim_supported: In the continental United States, UV rays tend to be strongest from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. during daylight saving time, and cloudy conditions do not eliminate UV exposure.
candidate.source_locator: Practice sun safety: continental U.S. UV rays strongest 10 a.m.-4 p.m. daylight saving time (9 a.m.-3 p.m. standard time); protection is important all year and UV rays can reach people on cloudy and cool days
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A client in the continental United States asks when solar ultraviolet (UV) rays tend to be strongest during daylight saving time. Which response by the nurse is correct?
